slides.title: Syntax & Letter-Writing
slides.subtitle: Lesson 17 · The Rules & the Friendly Letter

slides.heading: Syntax & Its Rules
bullets: Syntax is the part of grammar that treats the construction of sentences.
A Rule of Syntax states how words should be used together.
Harvey gives twenty rules — they are the reasons we give when we parse.
The most useful ones are about case and about agreement.

slides.heading: The Case Rules
bullets: A subject or a predicate noun is in the nominative case:  “Boys skate.”  “Horses are animals.”
The object of a verb or a preposition is in the objective case:  “hunt buffaloes,” “over the bridge.”
A noun showing ownership is in the possessive case:  “John’s hat.”
A noun used independently is in the nominative absolute:  “James, come here.”

slides.heading: Practice — Which Case?
slides.instruction: Tell the case of the noun or pronoun in parentheses.

slides.heading: The Agreement Rules
bullets: A verb agrees with its subject in person and number:  “He runs,” “they run.”
Two singular subjects joined by and take a plural verb:  “Tom and Sue are here.”
A pronoun agrees with its antecedent in gender, person, and number.
An adjective or participle belongs to some noun or pronoun.

slides.heading: Practice — Fix the Agreement
slides.instruction: Each sentence has an agreement mistake. Give the correct verb.

slides.heading: The Parts of a Letter
bullets: Heading — your town and the date, at the top right:  “Boston, Mass., May 1, 2026.”
Greeting — whom you write to:  “Dear Grandma,”
Body — the message itself, in clear sentences.
Closing & Signature — “Yours truly,” then your name.

slides.heading: Addressing the Envelope
bullets: Write the name of the person on the first line:  “Mr. James Johnson.”
Then the street, then the city and state (and country, if far away).
Put the stamp in the upper right-hand corner.
Write everything plainly — a smudged address may never arrive.

slides.heading: Practice — Parts of a Letter
slides.instruction: Tell which part of a letter each belongs to: heading, greeting, body, closing, or signature.
items: I hope you are well and happy.
